subject: Geography
topic: Indian and world lakes — mixed tiers
description: Largest, deepest, brackish, glacial, oxbow — Indian + world examples

questions.stem: The largest freshwater lake in India by area is:

options.option_text: Chilika (Odisha)
Wular Lake (Jammu & Kashmir)
Loktak (Manipur)
Vembanad (Kerala)

questions.explanation: Wular — largest freshwater lake in India, 30-260 km² (varies seasonally), in Bandipora district, J&K, fed by River Jhelum. Chilika (Odisha) is the largest LAGOON / brackish-water lake (1,165 km²). Vembanad (Kerala) is the longest lake (96 km), used for the famous Nehru Trophy snake-boat race. Loktak (Manipur) is famous for its floating phumdis. Wular is also a Ramsar site (1990).

questions.stem: The world's deepest freshwater lake — containing about 22% of Earth's surface freshwater — is:

options.option_text: Lake Superior
Lake Baikal (Russia)
Lake Tanganyika
Caspian Sea

questions.explanation: Lake Baikal — Siberia, Russia. Maximum depth 1,642 m (~1.6 km — deepest freshwater lake). Holds ~23,615 km³ water = ~22% of world's surface freshwater. UNESCO WHS 1996. ~25 million years old (oldest existing lake). Endemic species — Baikal seal (Pusa sibirica), the only freshwater seal. Caspian Sea is the largest lake (by area, 371,000 km²) but is brackish. Tanganyika — 2nd deepest (1,470 m) and 2nd by volume. Superior is the largest by surface area among freshwater lakes (82,000 km²).

questions.topic: Indian and world lakes — mixed tiers

options.option_text: Glacial erosion
A meandering river that gets cut off when the meander loop is severed
Volcanic crater filling with rainwater
Tectonic subsidence

questions.explanation: Oxbow lake — crescent-shaped (named for the U-bend of an ox's yoke). Formation: a river meander loops tighter and tighter; eventually the river cuts a new direct channel across the neck of the loop; the abandoned bend becomes a still-water U-shaped lake. Common on flat floodplains — Ganga, Brahmaputra, Ravi all have many oxbow lakes. Glacial lakes (cirque, tarn) form by glacier carving; crater lakes by volcanic activity (e.g. Lonar Lake, Maharashtra, ~50,000 yrs old, formed by meteorite impact in basalt).

questions.stem: Lonar Lake — a circular saline-soda lake of meteoritic origin, ~50,000 years old, is in:

options.option_text: Tamil Nadu
Maharashtra (Buldhana district)
Madhya Pradesh
Karnataka

questions.explanation: Lonar Lake — Buldhana district, Maharashtra. Formed by a meteorite impact in basalt rock ~52,000 years ago — making it the only known hypervelocity impact crater in basalt on Earth. Diameter ~1.2 km; maximum depth 137 m. Both saline AND alkaline (a rare combination). Declared a Ramsar site in 2020. Near Aurangabad — about 175 km. Geologically and astrobiologically significant; ISRO and NASA have studied the site.

questions.stem: Match lake with state — which pairing is INCORRECT?

options.option_text: Sambhar — Rajasthan
Pulicat — Andhra Pradesh / Tamil Nadu border
Kolleru — Karnataka
Dal — Jammu & Kashmir

questions.explanation: Kolleru is in ANDHRA PRADESH (between the deltas of Krishna and Godavari) — NOT Karnataka. Largest freshwater lake in Andhra; declared Ramsar site 2002; key habitat for migratory pelicans, painted storks. Sambhar — largest INLAND saline lake in India (Rajasthan). Pulicat — second largest brackish-water lagoon (after Chilika), AP-TN border. Dal — Srinagar, J&K, famous for shikaras + houseboats.

questions.stem: The largest lake in the world by area (though technically a lake, sometimes called a sea) is:

options.option_text: Lake Superior
Caspian Sea
Lake Victoria
Lake Baikal

questions.explanation: Caspian Sea — endorheic (no outlet), 371,000 km² — bordered by 5 countries (Russia, Kazakhstan, Turkmenistan, Iran, Azerbaijan). Brackish. Often called a 'sea' because of its size and salt content (~1.2%, about a third of seawater). Lake Superior is the largest FRESHWATER lake by area (82,100 km²). Lake Victoria — Africa, 2nd largest freshwater by area (68,800 km²); Tanganyika — 2nd longest. The 'lake vs sea' status of the Caspian was settled by the 2018 Convention as a 'special status' body, neither fully sea nor fully lake.

questions.stem: The Tso Lhamo / Tso Lhamu Lake — claimed to be one of the highest lakes in the world (~5,330 m) — is in:

options.option_text: Ladakh
Sikkim (North district, near Tibetan border)
Himachal Pradesh
Uttarakhand

questions.explanation: Tso Lhamo — North Sikkim, ~5,330 m above sea level, source of the Teesta River. Located near the China border; visit requires special permits. The fresh water of the lake is fed by glaciers and snowmelt. Other notable Sikkim lakes — Gurudongmar (5,210 m, sacred to Sikhs/Hindus/Buddhists), Tsomgo (3,750 m, popular tourism). Himalayan high-altitude lakes are sensitive indicators of climate change. Pangong Tso (Ladakh, 4,350 m) and Tso Moriri (4,522 m) are larger but lower than Tso Lhamo.

questions.stem: Which of the following correctly identifies Sambhar Salt Lake?

options.option_text: Largest freshwater lake in India, located in Rajasthan
Largest inland saltwater lake in India, located in Rajasthan
Largest coastal brackish-water lagoon in Asia, located in Gujarat
Largest high-altitude saline lake in India, located in Ladakh

questions.explanation: Sambhar Salt Lake in Rajasthan is India's largest inland saltwater lake (area ~190–230 km² seasonally) and a Ramsar Wetland site since 1990. Option A is wrong — Wular Lake (J&K) holds the freshwater title. Option C describes Chilika Lake in Odisha, not Gujarat. Option D describes Pangong Tso in Ladakh, which is saline but far smaller and high-altitude — a common mix-up.

questions.stem: Pangong Tso, the high-altitude lake in Ladakh, is correctly described by which of the following statements?

options.option_text: It is entirely within Indian territory and feeds the Indus river
It is a freshwater lake and the highest lake in India by altitude
It is a saline lake extending approximately 60% into Chinese territory
It is the source of the Shyok river that eventually joins the Indus

questions.explanation: Pangong Tso is a saline, endorheic (no outlet) lake spanning ~134 km; roughly 45 km lies in India and ~89 km (≈60–65%) in Tibet Autonomous Region of China. Option B is wrong — it is saline, not freshwater. Option A is wrong — the lake crosses the Line of Actual Control. Option D is wrong — Pangong Tso has no outflow; the Shyok is an independent Indus tributary unconnected to the lake.

questions.stem: The floating masses of vegetation, soil, and organic matter called 'phumdis' are the defining ecological feature of which Indian lake?

options.option_text: Chilika Lake in Odisha — Asia's largest brackish coastal lagoon
Loktak Lake in Manipur — largest freshwater lake in northeast India
Kolleru Lake in Andhra Pradesh — Ramsar wetland fed by Krishna-Godavari
Wular Lake in Jammu & Kashmir — a tectonic lake in the Kashmir Valley

questions.explanation: Loktak Lake (Manipur) is famous for phumdis — heterogeneous floating masses of soil, vegetation, and organic matter unique to this lake. The Keibul Lamjao National Park, the world's only floating national park, rests on these phumdis. Chilika is a coastal lagoon with no phumdis. Kolleru and Wular are freshwater lakes without this feature — Chilika is often confused because it too is a prominent Ramsar site.

questions.stem: Lake Titicaca, often described as the world's highest commercially navigable lake at ~3,800 m above sea level, straddles the border between which two countries?

options.option_text: Chile and Argentina — both sharing the southern Andes cordillera
Peru and Bolivia — sharing the high Altiplano plateau of South America
Ecuador and Colombia — both located in the northern Andes highland belt
Brazil and Paraguay — sharing the South American interior lowland border

questions.explanation: Lake Titicaca lies on the Altiplano between Peru (northwest shore) and Bolivia (southeast shore) at ~3,812 m. It is also the largest lake in South America by water volume. The most tempting distractor is Chile-Bolivia, since Bolivia is landlocked and frequently associated with Chile geographically — but Chilean territory does not touch the lake. Ecuador and Colombia are northern-Andes nations far from Titicaca.

questions.stem: Kolleru Lake, a Ramsar Wetland of International Importance in Andhra Pradesh, is naturally situated between the deltas of which two river systems?

options.option_text: Mahanadi and Godavari — large rivers flowing through Odisha and AP
Krishna and Godavari — two major peninsular rivers of Andhra Pradesh
Tungabhadra and Krishna — rivers originating in the Deccan plateau
Pennar and Godavari — rivers along the northern Andhra coastal belt

questions.explanation: Kolleru Lake is a large freshwater lake located between the deltas of the Krishna (to its south) and Godavari (to its north) in the West Godavari and Krishna districts of Andhra Pradesh; declared a Ramsar site in 2002. The Mahanadi drains through Odisha and is entirely unrelated to Kolleru. The Tungabhadra is a Krishna tributary inland on the Deccan, not a delta-framing river for Kolleru.

questions.stem: Lake Vostok, buried beneath approximately 4 km of ice in East Antarctica, is scientifically significant primarily because it is:

options.option_text: A meteoritic crater lake with the most acidic water recorded on Earth
A subglacial lake sealed from the atmosphere for an estimated 15–25 million years
The world's largest periglacial kettle lake formed by retreating glaciers
A tectonic rift lake with the deepest known lake floor at roughly 3,800 m depth

questions.explanation: Lake Vostok is the largest known subglacial lake (~250 km long, ~50 km wide) in Antarctica, isolated under ~3.7–4 km of ice for an estimated 15–25 million years. It is an astrobiology target because extremophile life may have persisted in its cold, high-pressure, oxygen-rich waters. Option D confuses Vostok with Lake Baikal (world's deepest at ~1,642 m). It is neither a meteoritic nor a periglacial feature; the ice above it formed long after the lake was sealed.

questions.stem: The Keibul Lamjao National Park — the world's only floating national park — rests on the phumdis of Loktak Lake and is the last natural refuge of which critically threatened species?

options.option_text: Barasingha (swamp deer) — state animal of Madhya Pradesh, found in wetlands
Sangai (brow-antlered deer) — state animal of Manipur, called the dancing deer
Hangul (Kashmir stag) — state animal of Jammu & Kashmir, a Cervus elaphus subspecies
Chital (spotted deer) — widely distributed across Indian forests and grasslands

questions.explanation: The Sangai (Rucervus eldii eldii), or Eld's deer, is the state animal of Manipur and is popularly called the 'dancing deer' because its unusual gait on soft, spongy phumdis makes it appear to dance. Keibul Lamjao is its only surviving wild habitat. The Barasingha is protected in Kanha (MP) and Dudhwa (UP) — a common distractor since both are swamp-associated deer. The Hangul survives in Dachigam NP, Jammu & Kashmir. Chital is common and widespread, not specific to Keibul.
